title: Polyinference · merged agent architecture
description: Original node names and spatial layout, expanded architecture contracts and connections, and the original unmodified data and memory model.

nodes.title: Cloud Model · senior engineer
nodes.subtitle: CLOUD PIPE / STRATEGY
nodes.body: One cloud-model node owns all senior work. Its prompt changes with the invocation reason, rather than creating a separate node for each prompt. INITIAL: receive the user objective, repository snapshot, acceptance criteria, and run limits; interpret the project and propose a first sprint. SPRINT REVIEW: compare planned work with task reports, commits, and test evidence; explain what went well and wrong, revise assumptions, and assign the next sprint. SPECIALIST TASK: occasionally solve an explicitly assigned difficult problem using the same bounded tool and evidence contracts as the local worker. COMPLETION REVIEW: decide whether project-level verification is justified. The first model inference in a new run is always here. this box defines the role and prompt mode; inference happens through Query Processor → Cloud process entry → Cloud conductor. It is not a second paid call before the OS entry. Specialist actions, observations, verification and repairs use the shared evidence boundary.
facts: Think of this model as the senior engineer and the sprint meeting. It is called at sprint boundaries or concrete exceptions, not after every local action.
A planning response contains a short sprint goal and scoped work items: task ID, dependencies, base revision, allowed tools, instructions, acceptance checks, local/cloud role, and attempt limits.

Review prompts receive a bounded retrospective packet with successful/failed work, observations, tests, checkpoint SHAs, unresolved risks, queue state, and remaining resources; full traces remain retrievable artifacts.
Review, planning, difficult-task execution, and completion use modes of this same node. A single response can review the previous sprint and plan the next.

The common inference gateway enforces context fit, sharing policy, endpoint health, retries, usage accounting, and reserved cloud budget. Required cloud access that is unavailable pauses or stops the run honestly.
pressure may request an explicit eligible assignment change, never silently weaken criteria or role authority.

contract.input: invocation_reason: initial | sprint_review | plan_correction | specialist_task | specialist_observation | specialist_repair | completion_review; objective; evidence_refs; remaining_budget
contract.output: sprint plan + retrospective | bounded specialist action/candidate | completion_candidate | blocked

nodes.title: Project acceptance
nodes.subtitle: DELIVERY
nodes.body: The senior proposes project completion after reviewing local results. Check current project criteria and the reviewed resulting revision. A local successful verdict is not project completion. Pending steering is applied at its prescribed planner boundary; queue exhaustion alone does not prove success. Run the independent integration/regression checks required by the project through Tools & observations. Complete only when both the senior decision and current host evidence support it. Failed checks return concrete evidence to ORCHESTRATOR / LOOP HANDLER for another review. Persist truthful blocked, budget_stopped, failed or cancelled outcomes with partial work and continuation references.
facts: An exhausted sprint queue triggers a retrospective; it is not project completion.
Task-level success does not prove the combined system works. Unavailable or stale required checks cannot yield completed.
Persist integrated commit references, checks, unresolved backlog/risks, and separate cloud/local resource accounting.
No model call is needed simply to announce a hard budget stop. Resumable interruptions retain their continuation and partial branches.

contract.input: senior completion proposal + reviewed revision/evidence + current planning state
contract.output: project outcome with evidence, or concrete review issues

nodes.title: Local coding agent loop
nodes.subtitle: OS / LOCAL PIPE
nodes.body: Run in this process's private code copy. Ordinary implementation reasoning and non-shell edits can overlap other agents. Every shell operation uses shell_mutex. Before final testing, request verification ownership, merge latest head and run the special reconciliation development loop. The final one/few local iterations test/examine/assess. A repair inside verification returns to development, then final assessment again. All phases and allowances are explicit.

contract.input: private workspace; phase=development|reconciliation|assessment; observations; token refs; bounds
contract.output: inference/action proposal; candidate requesting verification; assessment evidence/verdict

nodes.title: Tools & observations
nodes.subtitle: OS / LOCAL PIPE
nodes.body: Run tools against the declared process copy. Every shell/script action requires current shell_mutex ownership, including commands during reconciliation, assessment or commit. Non-shell private edits do not need a global coding lock. Return paired observations and relevant completion/effect state. Release shell only after the operation and relevant background effects ended; shared external resources need explicit scope/conflict rules.
facts: Authorization, exact-operation human decisions when required, process/environment isolation, and operation IDs are host responsibilities.
Pair results and denials with their call IDs; spool full output into artifacts and pass a bounded observation to the model.
Record exit codes, timings, usage, mutation metadata, and current tree. Edits invalidate affected evidence.
Tool errors are observations. Repeated errors or no progress close the bounded attempt instead of looping forever.
Inspect ambiguous mutation/timeout outcomes before replay. If effects cannot be established, preserve state and pause.
Task/project verification uses this same guarded runtime internally; it does not need another model call merely to read an exit status.

contract.input: scoped action; workspace; shell token if shell; phase/operation identity
contract.output: paired observation + revision/effects + confirmed/unknown completion

nodes.title: Task verification
nodes.subtitle: OS / LOCAL PIPE
nodes.body: The last one/few local LLM loops assess the reconciled private tree while verification_gate remains owned. Run tests/examination through the same local inference/tools path; shell commands take shell_mutex individually. Assessment produces fail, uncertain or successful. Any repair requires another final assessment. Missing assessment means interrupted/assessment-pending, not normal completion. The host independently validates the required check records against the exact assessed tree. Unavailable, stale or missing required evidence cannot yield successful. Blocked, budget-exhausted and interrupted attempts retain their explicit stopping state; they are not silently converted into an assessed normal completion.
facts: Record command, availability/status, exit code, output artifact, and tested tree/revision for each check.
The assigned model performs the final examination; the host enforces the acceptance criteria and evidence contract.
A repair retains the assigned role and verification ownership, and requires final assessment again.

contract.input: verification token; reconciled tree; assessment prompt/evidence; remaining allowance
contract.output: assessment_complete + fail|uncertain|successful + exact tree/evidence

nodes.title: Commit & task report
nodes.subtitle: LOCAL PIPE / RETURN
nodes.body: Before releasing verification ownership, create the attributable agent commit P and publish provisional_head=P with the immutable unresolved report. Prefer parent(P)=captured H and the final assessed tree so senior revert undoes this agent's net delta, not incoming predecessor changes. Retain original B/private merge history as evidence. Every normally completed verdict, including fail/uncertain, publishes provisionally with hazards and remains unresolved. Publication is not senior approval; a private-only commit is insufficient for the next agent.
facts: Record task/attempt identity, original base B, captured predecessor H, tested tree, actual checkpoint SHA, evidence, usage and unresolved issues.
A no-diff normal completion may use an empty metadata commit; never fabricate a SHA when Git fails or its outcome is uncertain.
Tests remain bound to their exact tree. Changed content requires new checks, even if a model claims success.
All normal assessed outcomes publish provisionally and remain unresolved until senior review.
Crash, incomplete assessment or uncertain publication requires reconciliation before closure or ownership release.

contract.input: verification token; B; captured H; final assessed tree; verdict/evidence; actual commit P
contract.output: durable provisional_head=P + execution=completed,resolution=unresolved report; then gate release

nodes.title: Cloud process entry
nodes.subtitle: OS
nodes.body: durable ready/admission queue for cloud processes, distinct from the worker Task Queue. Validate caller, grant, versions, required capabilities and limits. Waiting for quota does not occupy a host thread or imply that a provider job has begun. Dispatch admitted work to the existing cloud conductor.

contract.input: CloudProcessSpec + expected control/binding versions
contract.output: ready/waiting receipt → conductor; or typed invalid/unsupported/denied result

nodes.title: Cloud Query Processor
nodes.subtitle: CLOUD PIPE
nodes.body: build one versioned CloudProcessSpec from the selected senior prompt mode or claimed cloud-specialist task. Include bounded context/evidence refs, expected output schema, required model_inference/agent_job execution kind, allowed tools/providers, fallback policy, priority, finite limits, binding version, stable logical-step identity and return target. Submit it to the OS; this is packaging, not a model call.

contract.input: invocation reason + pinned project/task/steering/context refs + allowed binding/limits
contract.output: validated CloudProcessSpec + stable process/operation identity

nodes.title: Task Queue
nodes.subtitle: LOCAL PIPE
nodes.body: Worker-task ledger: pending, in-progress and completed-unresolved processes. Each started agent owns a private copy. Provisional shared publication occurs inside verification ownership before release, including fail/uncertain commits with hazards; it never resolves the report. Only sprint-coordinator review resolves outputs. Steering stops new starts and waits for already-in-progress local agents, including lock waiters, then goes to the planner. Pending unstarted queue items do not need to finish.
facts: All normal completions remain unresolved, including successful.
Provisional head and reviewed disposition are separate.
Original base, captured head, assessed tree and published commit remain attributable.

contract.input: TaskSpecs; completed unresolved TaskReports; senior dispositions; steering dispatch gate
contract.output: claimed task; unresolved result history; pending work; dependency/hazard context

nodes.title: ORCHESTRATOR / LOOP HANDLER
nodes.subtitle: MASTER
nodes.body: Program-level control for the agent design. The LLM OS operates LLM/tool endpoints; it does not integrate with Linux or enter computer-kernel space. Record steering and stop new local starts, but let the captured currently-in-progress local agents finish their original implementation, final assessment, commit and unresolved report. Then invoke the sprint planner to apply steering and resolve outputs. The pending task queue does not have to finish. Keep control/status/completion handling active while shell/verification ownership is held.
facts: Steering does not change running agents' goals or task specifications.
A started local agent waiting on inference/tools/the coding gate is in progress. Pending unstarted queue tasks are excluded.
All completed local processes remain unresolved until sprint-coordinator review, including successful ones.

contract.input: objective; queue/report events; pressure; pending steering + captured running-local IDs
contract.output: typed dispatch/planning requests; drain bookkeeping; resume/status; reviewed dispositions

nodes.title: Result Processor
nodes.subtitle: CLOUD PIPE
nodes.body: Normalize cloud plan/review proposals and specialist results. Validate scope, schema, limits and actual accepted plan versions. Review decisions identify the completed-unresolved agent report and commit, then route to Senior resolution for keep/revert/retry/defer. Initial/next plans update the queue. Steering receipt alone does not invalidate running local agents' original plan or reports: the sprint planner applies pending steering only after the captured running-local set finishes. A completion proposal goes to Project acceptance.
facts: All local verdicts require sprint-coordinator resolution.
Notes are versioned context; tool grants and code review remain explicit.
Steering input sequence differs from accepted plan revision.

contract.input: typed cloud result + accepted plan/head versions + unresolved reports + planner input range
contract.output: validated plan | senior resolution decision | specialist action/candidate | completion proposal

nodes.title: Local inference
nodes.subtitle: OS / INFERENCE
nodes.body: Shared local inference service, one component of the OS. accept a bounded prompt and stable operation identity, check context fit and shared memory/decode admission, execute the configured model, and return a typed output to Result Processor (OS / LOCAL PIPE). This component does not independently authorize tools, change task scope, verify completion or become the whole OS.

contract.input: prompt/context refs + limits + operation/binding identity
contract.output: model output/action proposal + actual model/version + usage + typed status

nodes.title: Result Processor
nodes.subtitle: OS / LOCAL PIPE
nodes.body: Interpret model/tool output with process workspace and phase. Private non-shell edits use only their workspace scope; shell proposals request shell_mutex. An ordinary development candidate requests verification_gate, not direct final assessment. After merge/reconciliation development, enter final assessment under the same gate. Only completed final assessment produces fail/uncertain/successful for commit/report. No verdict resolves the task.

contract.input: phase-aware output/observation + private workspace + ownership refs
contract.output: private continuation | shell request | verification entry | assessment result

nodes.title: Info Documentation
nodes.subtitle: DOCS
nodes.body: retain report change briefs and final queue dispositions, including cancellations, in a deduplicated durable backlog. At a batch threshold or senior review, capture an input range and accepted code revision. If generation is needed, enqueue a bounded doc-update task through Task Queue, rather than writing into an active worker workspace. Publish a new doc version and advance the consumed cursor together; failed updates keep the backlog. Workers use pinned versions or explicit unprocessed deltas.
facts: The backlog survives interruption even before a model-generated update exists.
Do not make a doc update recursively wait on consuming its own report.
Summary text cannot rewrite grants, evidence or accepted history.

contract.input: report/disposition events + current docs + captured code revision + batch cursor
contract.output: bounded doc TaskSpec OR versioned docs + acknowledged event range

nodes.title: USER PROMPT
nodes.subtitle: CUSTOM STATE
nodes.body: Long running prompt by the user to be worked on The initial objective enters ORCHESTRATOR / LOOP HANDLER. Later steering is recorded in Immediate Memory and applied by the sprint planner after the captured running local tasks finish.

contract.input: initial objective, acceptance criteria and run limits; subsequent ordered steering
contract.output: initial run request; durable pending-steering event

nodes.title: Cloud conductor / loop
nodes.subtitle: OS / CLOUD RUNTIME
nodes.body: execute the declared protocol. An agent endpoint uses its native session/turn/job lifecycle. A raw LLM uses a bounded host action/observation loop where the task requires agentic behavior; a structured planning query may use one generation. Never pretend a raw reply is an autonomous job and never nest a competing tool loop around an existing agent harness. report account-wide quota/rate/spend/health pressure with observation time and unknown fields. Enforce allowed overflow and stable submission/reconciliation rules. Specialist tools use the shared guarded boundary or an adapter contract with equivalent scope and evidence.
facts: Subscription quota windows are provider-reported/configured, not universally five-hour/weekly/monthly.
One mutable session operation at a time; all OS-managed processes share account admission.
A timeout/interrupt request does not prove the external job stopped.
Resume or rebind only at a supported settled boundary; retain unknown effects and accounting.

contract.input: admitted CloudProcessSpec | specialist observation/repair + operation/binding refs
contract.output: typed cloud step/terminal result; actual provider/model and usage; pressure snapshot; cancellation/uncertainty status

nodes.title: Immediate Memory
nodes.subtitle: AGENT DATA / OS STORAGE
nodes.body: Store objective, versioned notes/hazards and ordered steering. Steering is recorded now but applied later by the sprint planner. Signal the orchestrator to stop new local starts and capture currently-in-progress local IDs. Those agents finish on their old instructions; pending queue work does not run merely to empty the queue. Once captured agents have completed assessment/commit/report, send steering and unresolved results to the planner. The captured running set includes agents waiting for shell_mutex or verification_gate; those waiters must be allowed to enter and finish. Hazards track provisional fail/uncertain commits that later private copies merge.
facts: No immediate goal change, cancellation or replan on ordinary steering receipt.
New steering is retained by sequence/range; no lost input.
Hazards identify whether an unresolved change is present in current code or isolated elsewhere.

contract.input: objective; steering events; notes/hazard updates
contract.output: pending steering range; dispatch-gate signal; captured-running-set refs; pinned context

nodes.title: Trap frame mechanism
nodes.subtitle: OS / APPLICATION CONTINUATION
nodes.body: Persist private workspace/base, current development/reconciliation/assessment phase, captured shared head, both owner-token refs, pending shell/provider effects, commit/report/publication status and graph checkpoint. A crash or timeout does not prove protected work stopped. Reconcile effects and publication before releasing applicable exclusion or resuming. An old owner cannot publish without a fresh current-token/version check.

contract.input: process continuation + workspace/phase + both owners + pending effects/publication
contract.output: validated resume or explicit reconciliation wait/abort; no duplicated publication

nodes.title: Senior resolution / commit undo
nodes.subtitle: AGENT REVIEW / OS ACTIONS
nodes.body: Only sprint-coordinator review resolves completed reports. Keep/revert/retry/defer is separate from provisional shared publication and the local assessment verdict. A revert acquires verification_gate, takes shell_mutex for commands, checks later/dependent work and blast radius, then publishes its new head before release. Retain original/revert commit relationships. Git avoids reconstructing inverse edits but does not remove conflict/dependency analysis.

contract.input: senior decision; original/provisional commits; dependents; expected shared head
contract.output: review disposition + recorded keep/revert/retry/defer; resulting head/checks

nodes.title: Verification critical section
nodes.subtitle: OS / APPLICATION OWNERSHIP
nodes.body: One process at a time owns final reconciliation through shared publication. Acquire only after outside shell ownership is released. Capture latest provisional head H, merge it into the private copy, run at least one specially prompted development loop, then final assessment, commit and shared head/report publication before release. The coordinator remains active; other agents continue private development. Inside this section acquire shell_mutex individually for commands, always in verification→shell order.

contract.input: ready private candidate + task/process; no held outside shell token
contract.output: queued | verification owner token + captured H | reconciled release

nodes.title: Shell mutex · one command
nodes.subtitle: OS / APPLICATION OWNERSHIP
nodes.body: Every managed shell/script command uses one global shell mutex, even when agents have separate code copies. This includes Git/build/test commands invoked through shell. Release after actual relevant completion, not merely command launch or timeout. Outside verification, finish/release shell before requesting verification. Inside verification, acquire/release shell per command; do not hold it while reasoning. Native/remote agent shell work must be brokered or declared incompatible with this guarantee.

contract.input: shell request + process/workspace + optional verification token
contract.output: queued | sole shell owner + command result | release/unknown-effect wait

nodes.title: Private code copy · base B
nodes.subtitle: AGENT / PER-PROCESS WORKSPACE
nodes.body: Every in-progress coding agent gets its own codebase copy at a recorded base B. Private non-shell edits, context preparation and model reasoning can overlap. All tool requests identify this workspace. Start with full working trees; a partial copy requires dependency/build/test closure and a full-project mapping before publication.

contract.input: claimed task + process + base B + required project context
contract.output: private workspace/ref + scoped tool context

nodes.title: Merge head / reconciliation dev
nodes.subtitle: AGENT / VERIFICATION PHASE
nodes.body: While holding verification_gate, preserve the private pre-merge delta, merge current shared head H into this agent copy, resolve conflicts, and run at least one LLM development loop with a special prompt to inspect incoming changes and necessary adaptations. Run this even after a clean merge. Bound further repair work, then run final testing/examination/assessment. Shell operations still use shell_mutex individually.

contract.input: verification token; original B/private delta; latest H; task/observations
contract.output: updated private tree + reconciliation loop evidence -> final assessment

edges.label: Initial objective
edges.body: persist original objective, criteria and run limits. First inference is a cloud senior invocation.
edges.payload: objective_ref; criteria_ref; project grant/limits

edges.label: Invoke senior mode
edges.body: initial planning, sprint review, specialist assignment or completion review. Steering review carries the exact drained input range. This is a role invocation, not an inference before the query processor.
edges.payload: mode; report/context refs; expected plan/head/control epoch; steering range

edges.label: Build cloud process request
edges.body: prepare the selected prompt mode and return schema for OS execution.
edges.payload: invocation mode; required capabilities; scoped context/tools; finite limits

edges.label: Submit CloudProcessSpec
edges.body: create the durable logical cloud process and admission receipt.
edges.payload: CloudProcessSpec; stable identity; grant; binding/control versions

edges.label: Admit / run declared protocol
edges.body: route admitted cloud work to the existing conductor. Capacity wait is explicit; unknown submissions are reconciled before replacement.
edges.payload: process/operation refs; execution_kind; reservations

edges.label: Typed cloud step / result
edges.body: actual conductor output, not an unexecuted ready-queue response. Agent jobs and raw model loops normalize into declared result types.
edges.payload: plan/review | specialist_action | specialist_candidate | completion_candidate | blocked; usage/evidence

edges.label: Publish validated plan / dispositions
edges.body: publish validated plans and pending-task updates. Every completed local process still requires a coordinator review disposition; code keep/revert actions route through Senior resolution.
edges.payload: TaskSpecs; accepted plan revision; senior dispositions for pending work

edges.label: Senior reviews provisional commits
edges.body: review already-published unresolved work. Keep/revert/retry/defer is distinct from the previous publication.
edges.payload: published commits; verdicts; hazards; dependent work

edges.label: Store senior resolution
edges.body: publish the applied reviewed disposition and resulting code revision. No automatic task resolution by test result.
edges.payload: keep|revert|retry|defer; resolution record; commit/revert refs; checks

edges.label: Undo conflict / affected work
edges.body: expose revert conflict or questionable downstream work for senior examination.
edges.payload: original/revert commits; dependent work; conflict/check evidence

edges.label: Completion candidate
edges.body: a typed senior proposal reaches independent project checks; no direct success transition.
edges.payload: completion proposal; reviewed resulting revision; project criteria; pending-steering state

edges.label: Checks fail / stale completion
edges.body: return concrete project-check evidence for review. Pending steering waits for running locals and then goes to the planner; do not declare project completion over unprocessed steering.
edges.payload: project checks; current revision/epoch; unresolved risks

edges.label: Captured review state / versions
edges.body: replace undefined transition with host inputs used to validate a returned cloud decision. No model call occurs on this handoff.
edges.payload: report cursor; queue snapshot; expected plan/head/control epoch

edges.label: Completion / queue events
edges.body: every completed local process remains unresolved with its assessment verdict. Request sprint review on configured triggers; none auto-resolves because it is successful.
edges.payload: unresolved report IDs; fail|uncertain|successful; queue/dependency state

edges.label: Start with private code copy
edges.body: initialize each in-progress process with its own full copy/base and scoped tools; steering can stop new starts.
edges.payload: TaskSpec; process; B; workspace

edges.label: Claim cloud-specialist task
edges.body: worker-task ledger may contain an explicitly assigned specialist task. Preserve its identity and bounds through the cloud path; strategy requests never enter this queue.
edges.payload: claimed TaskSpec/attempt; cloud binding; scope/tools/checks

edges.label: Implementation / assessment prompt
edges.body: the same local endpoint runs implementation prompts and the final one or few testing/examination/assessment prompts.
edges.payload: phase=implementation|assessment; task; iteration; context/evidence; allowance

edges.label: Typed inference result
edges.body: interpret the result before any tool execution; a completion claim is not a shell action.
edges.payload: model output; operation identity; usage; status

edges.label: Shell action → global mutex
edges.body: every shell command across copies needs shell ownership. Private non-shell edits are a separate scoped path.
edges.payload: shell action; process/workspace; optional verification token

edges.label: Paired tool observation
edges.body: return one matched observation/denial and mutation metadata. The router retains the current task role.
edges.payload: call ID; result/exit code; output_ref; tree/mutation metadata

edges.label: Continue current local phase
edges.body: retain implementation or assessment mode. After implementation repair, final assessment is required again.
edges.payload: phase; observations; counters; owner token; remaining allowance

edges.label: Candidate → queue for verification
edges.body: outside shell ownership must be released before requesting verification. Final assessment is not entered before latest-head reconciliation.
edges.payload: private candidate; phase; no held shell token

edges.label: Repair under verification, reassess
edges.body: bounded development repairs retain verification ownership and must be followed by final assessment again.
edges.payload: phase=reconciliation; verification token; repair+assessment allowance

edges.label: Assessed → commit / publish unresolved
edges.body: every normal verdict publishes its attributable provisional commit and unresolved report before verification release.
edges.payload: fail|uncertain|successful; final tree/evidence; verification token

edges.label: Published, completed and unresolved
edges.body: provisional head and report are committed before gate release. Every verdict remains unresolved until senior review.
edges.payload: P; provisional_head; verdict; unresolved report/hazards

edges.label: Specialist shell → same mutex
edges.body: All managed specialist shell work obeys the same global broker; opaque uncontrolled shell endpoints are incompatible with this guarantee.
edges.payload: cloud task; scoped shell request

edges.label: Cloud specialist observation
edges.body: return the paired observation to the already-assigned cloud specialist process. Ordinary local errors do not use this edge.
edges.payload: active_role=cloud; same attempt/binding; observation/artifact refs; limits

edges.label: Cloud specialist candidate / stop
edges.body: cloud engineering work has the same final assessment and unresolved checkpoint/report closure as local work.
edges.payload: candidate/stop; task criteria; exact tree; provider evidence

edges.label: Cloud repair within allowance
edges.body: repair retains the cloud assignment and bounded shared harness contract.
edges.payload: active_role=cloud; check observations; remaining limits

edges.label: Quota / backpressure snapshot
edges.body: timestamped account-wide capacity/health/uncertainty informs deterministic orchestration. No invented exact remaining tokens from quota percentages.
edges.payload: PressureSnapshot; stale/unknown flags; reservations; queue age

edges.label: Dispatch / pressure policy
edges.body: normal pressure decisions use explicit safe points. Ordinary steering does not alter current agents: stop new local starts and finish the captured in-progress set first.
edges.payload: policy reason; task/binding versions; steering dispatch state

edges.label: Request captured doc batch
edges.body: replace undefined transition. At threshold or sprint review capture the input range; generation uses an ordinary bounded worker task.
edges.payload: event range; accepted code/doc versions; finite update limits

edges.label: Enqueue change brief
edges.body: durable deduplicated report/change event, retained before a summary is generated.
edges.payload: report ID; change summary; commit/evidence refs

edges.label: Final dispositions / history
edges.body: record resolution and cancellation without erasing the original report.
edges.payload: unique history event; task/spec/attempt; disposition

edges.label: Bounded documentation task
edges.body: queue an optional model-assisted doc update; no direct mutation of an active worker workspace.
edges.payload: captured backlog range; docs/code refs; TaskSpec; update bounds

edges.label: Pinned documentation / deltas
edges.body: immutable version and explicit pending delta range, not a half-updated shared file.
edges.payload: doc_version; artifact refs; unprocessed delta range

edges.label: Versioned senior notes
edges.body: proposed project-wide notes are host-published with sources and expected version.
edges.payload: note version; plan/report sources; bounded text

edges.label: Fail / uncertain / unresolved hazards
edges.body: record actual revision and blast radius, including unresolved code already present in v1 shared history.
edges.payload: agent commit; fail|uncertain|successful; unresolved status; affected scope

edges.label: Record steering for later planning
edges.body: append immediately; semantic application waits for the currently running local agents to finish.
edges.payload: ordered input range; pending steering

edges.label: Record steering / capture running locals
edges.body: stop new local starts; do not apply steering to current agents. Finish only the local process IDs already in progress, including those waiting on inference/tools/gate, then invoke the planner. Pending queue tasks do not have to finish.
edges.payload: pending input range; captured in-progress local IDs; completion reports

edges.label: Pinned notes / hazards
edges.body: bounded project context, distinct from current permissions and authoritative evidence. Urgent hazards can request a pause.
edges.payload: memory_version; source refs; hazard snapshot

edges.label: Pause / validated release
edges.body: reach a supported boundary, store a manifest and later revalidate/reconcile before resuming.
edges.payload: process; pause reason; expected versions; frame_ref

edges.label: Worker continuation refs
edges.body: checkpoint and operation identity/counters, never an assumed model-internal snapshot.
edges.payload: checkpoint; task/base/tree; pending effects; counters; bindings

edges.label: Cloud continuation refs
edges.body: include native session/job ID only with declared adapter resume/reconciliation support.
edges.payload: checkpoint; provider session/job; pending effects; reservations

edges.label: Final assessment iteration(s)
edges.body: same local LLM, phase=assessment, after post-merge development; verification ownership remains held.
edges.payload: phase=assessment; verification token; evidence; allowance

edges.label: Execute shell for sole owner
edges.body: the shell mutex admits exactly one command across all private copies.
edges.payload: shell token; process; workspace; operation

edges.label: Publish head/report, then release
edges.body: keep verification ownership until real commit and provisional head/unresolved report publication are durable; reconcile uncertainty before release.
edges.payload: captured H; P; report ref; publication/release state

edges.label: Acquire verification for senior undo
edges.body: senior revert serializes with reconciliation/testing/publication. Its shell commands also use shell_mutex; publish new head before release.
edges.payload: original commit; later dependents; expected H; review decision

edges.label: Private development can overlap
edges.body: agent reasons/edits only its own copy; shell commands still serialize.
edges.payload: workspace; B; task; phase=development

edges.label: Capture H / merge / re-examine
edges.body: while holding verification, merge latest provisional head and run at least one specially prompted development loop, even for a clean merge.
edges.payload: verification token; B/private delta; current H

edges.label: Special development prompt
edges.body: inspect incoming changes and necessary adaptations before final assessment; keep verification ownership.
edges.payload: phase=reconciliation; H; merged tree; special prompt

edges.label: Reconciled / assessment result
edges.body: this route requires verification ownership and completed post-merge development. Assessment output returns here with exact evidence.
edges.payload: phase; verification token; reconciliation_complete; evidence

edges.label: Non-shell edit in private copy
edges.body: only this process copy is edited; no global shell ownership needed for a non-shell operation.
edges.payload: workspace scope; non-shell action

edges.label: Confirmed command end → release
edges.body: release shell after relevant work/effects end; unknown/background effects preserve exclusion.
edges.payload: shell token; operation; result/effect certainty

edges.label: Inside: verification → shell only
edges.body: acquire/release shell individually for commands; never wait for verification while holding an outside shell token.
edges.payload: verification token; scoped command request

edges.label: Next entrant sees published P
edges.body: a private-only commit is insufficient; next verification owner captures updated provisional_head.
edges.payload: P; unresolved hazards; authoritative head

edges.label: Private state / merge provenance
edges.body: retain original B, workspace, pre-merge delta, captured H, phase, both owner refs and publication state.
edges.payload: workspace/base/head/phase refs

nodes.title: Cloud Model · senior engineer
nodes.subtitle: CLOUD PIPE / STRATEGY
nodes.body: One cloud-model node owns all senior work. Its prompt changes with the invocation reason, rather than creating a separate node for each prompt. INITIAL: receive the user objective, repository snapshot, acceptance criteria, and run limits; interpret the project and propose a first sprint. SPRINT REVIEW: compare planned work with task reports, commits, and test evidence; explain what went well and wrong, revise assumptions, and assign the next sprint. SPECIALIST TASK: occasionally solve an explicitly assigned difficult problem using the same bounded tool and evidence contracts as the local worker. COMPLETION REVIEW: decide whether project-level verification is justified. The first model inference in a new run is always here.
facts: Think of this model as the senior engineer and the sprint meeting. It is called at sprint boundaries or concrete exceptions, not after every local action.
A planning response contains a short sprint goal and scoped work items: task ID, dependencies, base revision, allowed tools, instructions, acceptance checks, local/cloud role, and attempt limits.

Review prompts receive a bounded retrospective packet with successful/failed work, observations, tests, checkpoint SHAs, unresolved risks, queue state, and remaining resources; full traces remain retrievable artifacts.
Review, planning, difficult-task execution, and completion use modes of this same node. A single response can review the previous sprint and plan the next.

The common inference gateway enforces context fit, sharing policy, endpoint health, retries, usage accounting, and reserved cloud budget. Required cloud access that is unavailable pauses or stops the run honestly.

contract.input: invocation_reason: initial | sprint_review | plan_correction | specialist_task | specialist_observation | specialist_repair | completion_review; objective; evidence_refs; remaining_budget
contract.output: sprint plan + retrospective | bounded specialist action/candidate | completion_candidate | blocked

nodes.title: Project acceptance
nodes.subtitle: DELIVERY
nodes.body: After the senior proposes completion, run the independent integration/regression checks required by the project against the integrated tree using the shared guarded tool runtime. Complete the project only when both the senior decision and current host evidence support it. Failed integration returns to the senior with concrete evidence for the next sprint. Also persist truthful blocked, budget_stopped, failed, or cancelled outcomes when the coordinator stops the run; these do not imply project success.
facts: An exhausted sprint queue triggers a retrospective; it is not project completion.
Task-level success does not prove the combined system works. Unavailable or stale required checks cannot yield completed.
Persist integrated commit references, checks, unresolved backlog/risks, and separate cloud/local resource accounting.
No model call is needed simply to announce a hard budget stop. Resumable interruptions retain their continuation and partial branches.

contract.input: senior completion_candidate + integrated tree + project criteria, OR explicit non-success stop reason
contract.output: completed + final_revision + evidence_refs, OR truthful non-success/paused status

nodes.title: Local coding agent loop
nodes.subtitle: OS / LOCAL PIPE
nodes.body: One local-model node performs each scoped assignment in a mini-swe-agent-style loop. Start with the leased task contract, repository rules, relevant context, and available tools. Propose the next tool action, inspect its returned observation, and repeat for a few bounded steps. A candidate, inability to continue, or exhausted allowance proceeds to host verification. Different task instructions and step prompts are modes of this same worker node, not separate agents.
facts: Local work includes implementation and tests. It is not restricted to read-only reconnaissance.
Each assignment has a fresh task transcript and explicit step/time/token limits; preserve complete tool-call/result pairs and artifact references when reducing context.
Tool errors and failed checks can be repaired locally while meaningful progress and allowance remain. No cloud review is needed for every ordinary failure.
The worker cannot expand its scope, rewrite sprint dependencies, or grant itself more budget. The host enforces these boundaries.
Malformed outputs receive bounded corrective feedback. Model confidence or a prose success claim never substitutes for check evidence.

contract.input: leased task + scope/base_sha + instructions/tools + observations + remaining task allowance
contract.output: tool proposal | completion_candidate | cannot_complete | budget_exhausted

nodes.title: Tools & observations
nodes.subtitle: OS / LOCAL PIPE
nodes.body: Host code validates the proposed tool and arguments, checks scope/authority and remaining limits, executes approved operations, records their effects and output, and returns a matched observation to the active task model. Use one shared runtime for search, reads, patches, commands, checks, and optional MCP tools. The normal active model is local; an explicitly assigned cloud specialist uses exactly this boundary and receives its own observations.
facts: Authorization, exact-operation human decisions when required, process/environment isolation, and operation IDs are host responsibilities.
Pair results and denials with their call IDs; spool full output into artifacts and pass a bounded observation to the model.
Record exit codes, timings, usage, mutation metadata, and current tree. Edits invalidate affected evidence.
Tool errors are observations. Repeated errors or no progress close the bounded attempt instead of looping forever.
Inspect ambiguous mutation/timeout outcomes before replay. If effects cannot be established, preserve state and pause.
Task/project verification uses this same guarded runtime internally; it does not need another model call merely to read an exit status.

contract.input: active task/model role + validated tool proposal + operation/input identity
contract.output: paired observation + exit status + output_ref + revision/mutation metadata + updated limits

nodes.title: Task verification
nodes.subtitle: OS / LOCAL PIPE
nodes.body: Run the assignment's configured acceptance checks through the shared guarded runtime, then compare the recorded evidence with the exact task tree. A meaningful repair may return to the model assigned to this task while its allowance remains. Otherwise close with passed, failed, blocked, or budget_exhausted. This evidence gate is shared by ordinary local tasks and the rare cloud specialist task.
facts: Record command, availability/status, exit code, output artifact, and checked tree/revision for each test.
No extra reviewer model is required to interpret a configured pass/fail criterion.
Missing required checks, stale evidence, or an unsupported success claim cannot produce passed.
A failed test with repair budget stays inside the task loop; an exhausted or unrecoverable attempt closes and is reported before sprint review.
Retain the assigned model role during repairs. Switching to cloud is a senior assignment decision, not an implicit fallback.

contract.input: candidate or stopping reason + task criteria + exact workspace tree + recorded checks
contract.output: repair observations + remaining allowance, OR verdict + tested_tree_id + evidence_refs

nodes.title: Commit & task report
nodes.subtitle: LOCAL PIPE / RETURN
nodes.body: Close every finished task attempt with an auditable checkpoint commit and a structured result packet. Commit only scoped changes to the task branch; a no-diff task uses a metadata-only empty commit. This applies to passed, failed, blocked, and budget-exhausted attempts. Record the real SHA before emitting the report, then return it to the sprint coordinator. The model may draft the observation, but host records supply the verdict, test facts, revision, and usage.
facts: Required packet fields: task/attempt ID, verdict, observation, test results, base SHA, checkpoint SHA, evidence refs, usage, and unresolved issues.
Passed work is only a candidate for integration. Failed or partial work remains reachable on its own branch.
Tie tests to the tested tree ID; a new commit of the identical tree may retain that evidence, while changed content requires new checks.
If Git fails or its outcome is uncertain, reconcile by task/attempt ID and inspect the branch. Do not fabricate a SHA.
A crash before a checkpoint can exist is an interrupted attempt, not a completed task. Resume/reconcile or retain an explicit paused status.

contract.input: closed verdict + scoped tree + tests + task/attempt identity
contract.output: { task_id, attempt_id, verdict, observation, tests:[{command,status,exit_code,revision,output_ref}], base_sha, commit_sha, evidence_refs, usage, blockers }

nodes.title: Cloud conductor / loop
nodes.subtitle: OS
nodes.body:
does a few things: 

if the cloud model is an agent subscription like claude pro or chatgpt plus or something alike: manages the 5h/week/monthly limit, route to overflow provider or stalls when limit reached (depending on priority setting of the task).

If the cloud model is a pure LLM API:
run a simple programmatic agent loop over it to match the agentic assumption of the query. This can be implemented later (in the prototyping version, if the cloud endpoint is pure llm, just pretend its an agent anyways)

nodes.body:
IMPLEMENT IN LATER VERSIONS, IGNORE IN FIRST VERSION!!

Stores the state of the machine once in a while and statically. Prep for crash recovery.

edges.label: Project wide observations and notes
edges.body: Written and updated by each sprint manager process, fed into context of each local agent loop. Short and concise

edges.label: Failure and uncertain cases
edges.body: For each task completed that's not full successful (uncertain or failure): write a note in the memory to warn other local workers that this agent's blast radius and that things around its work is unstable

edges.label: Queue history
edges.body: write the final state of each item in the queue to the documentation. If an item is cancelled by the sprint manager, it's written in as "cancelled"

edges.label: Project doc change
edges.body: Send the agent's change to the documentation manager as a highly summarized brief. The doc manager will update the project docs accordingly and in batch

edges.label: Injects user steering
edges.body: once user steering received and OS finished all running processes, the user steering is sent to the model to be included in the sprint management decisions.

edges.label: use
edges.body: use the conductor to optimize cloud querying. This should be an OS feature

edges.label: Inform
edges.body:
Tells the orchestrator the upcoming volume of the cloud providers. 

In time of high back pressure, the orchestrator should stall lower priority tasks and/or downgrade lower fidelity tasks

In time of low back pressure (especially if it's a monthly subscription instead of a cost-per-token model), the orchestrator should upgrade important tasks (route more tasks to the "senior dev" with the cloud model to improve performance. It should also release stalled processes into the system for execution. There may be very low priority tasks given by the user like "parse this codebase an generate a graph structure for it". Those should be released in time of least system pressure.

edges.label: Pressure aware task orchestration
edges.body: Using the info given by the cloud conductor, the orchestrator would stall, release, upgrade (give instruction for more tasks done by cloud model) or downgrade tasks. Note that a task may be upgraded or downgraded or stalled even if its already released into the system.
edges.payload: THis requires the process data struct to be able to handle all these info. There should be a trap frame store/load mechanism for context switching

edges.body: Stores all the task reports not yet processed or reflected for documentation

edges.body: usually the trap should let an agent finish. In case of otherwise (error/emergency/etc), this is added to the trap frame. In fetching time, check whether an agent is stored
